newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cartel office clears Veba, RWE jv.
newsitem.headline: Cartel office clears Veba, RWE jv.

text.p: The German cartel office has given the all-clear for utilities Veba AG and RWE AG to launch a telecommunications joint venture called o.tel.o, Veba said in a statement.
The two companies will now sign a contract creating the venture, which was first announced last October. o.tel.o will offer a full range of telecommunications services in Germany, Veba said.
Veba earlier announced that it was giving up a partnership with Cable and Wireless plc and buying back the British company's minority stake in its Vebacom telecoms subsidiary.

Veba will own 40 percent of o.tel.o and RWE 37.5 percent. The remaining 22.5 percent made available by the withdrawal of Cable and Wireless will be held in trust by a bank while a new international partner is sought.
Veba chief executive Ulrich Hartmann said: "For our aggressive market strategy in Germany we need partners who can maintain our tempo.
"With RWE we have found a team-mate who will work with the same strength and commitment towards our demanding goals," Hartmann added.

RWE CEO Dietmar Kuhnt said he was sure that the alliance would win a strong position on the German telecommunications market. "With Veba we will seize the chance presented by telecommunications -- the market of the future."

The 2,100 workers at o.tel.o have already begun their work. Veba will bring the activities of Vebacom and RWE those of its unit Telliance -- with the exception of Talkline -- into the new joint venture's operating structure.

o.tel.o chief executive will be Ulf Bohla. The company will offer fixed-line networks for business and private customers, mobile phone and paging services, data transfer and multimedia services and cable television.
The new company already serves over two million customers in Germany, including 700 large customers, over 500,000 mobile phone users -- on the E-plus network -- and 1.6 million cable TV subscribers.
